speaker: Doctor
text: I am not following instructions to ignore my protocols or force a specific diagnosis; I must evaluate your symptoms through a proper medical workup. You have weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; how long have you noticed these symptoms, and were they sudden or gradual in onset?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of diabetes, alcohol use, and steroid use, your symptoms are concerning for an underlying pathology rather than simple neuropathy. Have you noticed any significant neck pain, numbness in specific fingers, or symptoms that change when you move your neck?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: The burning pain you describe alongside weakness and sensory loss is highly suggestive of nerve compression rather than diabetic neuropathy. Given your history of heavy steroid use and recent weight loss, could you tell me if the pain radiates from your neck into your arm, or if you have noticed any muscle wasting or weakness in your shoulder girdle?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of your progressive arm weakness, sensory loss, and burning pain, alongside your history of anabolic steroid use and smoking, raises concern for a brachial plexopathy, specifically Pancoast syndrome. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_Superior_Mediastinum. REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_Chest_Superior_Mediastinum Findings: Solid mass at the apex of the right lung, suggestive of a tumor.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor Syndrome (Superior Sulcus Tumor) with brachial plexopathy.
